output.body:
# HPID, healthcare professional identifier

## In plain words

Healthcare Professional ID: a 14 digit number issued to a healthcare
professional or a facility manager after Aadhaar authentication. It is
the professional's digital identity across ABDM, and it is created on
the [HPR](hpr.md). See [M4](/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#m4).

## Before you start

Nothing. A glossary entry assumes no prior reading.

## What happens

Nothing happens here. This entry defines a term, it does not describe a call.

## How you know it worked

You have understood this when you can say who an HPID is issued to and where it is created.

## When it goes wrong

Expecting the number before Aadhaar authentication. NHA issues it after
that step, so anything needing an HPID cannot run first.
output.summary: A 14 digit number issued to a healthcare professional or a facility manager, created on the HPR.
output.title: HPID, healthcare professional identifier

output.body:
# HPR, Healthcare Professionals Registry

## In plain words

HPR holds verified healthcare professionals: doctors from every system
of medicine, meaning modern medicine, dentistry, Ayurveda, Unani,
Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa and homeopathy, along with nurses and pharmacists.
Registration issues a Healthcare Professional ID, which acts as the
professional's identity across ABDM.

Enrolment is voluntary and free. It does not replace the registration a
professional already holds with their council. The councils remain the
authority, and HPR verifies against them.

HPR and the Health Facility Registry together make up the National
Healthcare Professionals and Facilities Registry, NHPR, which is
milestone M4. Both
`hpr.abdm.gov.in` and `facility.abdm.gov.in` now redirect to
`nhpr.abdm.gov.in`.

## Before you start

Nothing. A glossary entry assumes no prior reading.

## What happens

Nothing happens here. This entry defines a term, it does not describe a call.

## How you know it worked

You have understood this when you can say what HPR is without using the acronym itself.

## When it goes wrong

HPR runs on a different host and a different API version from M1 to M3, so credentials and base URLs do not carry across.

The identifier is spelled three ways across NHA's own pages: Healthcare
Professional ID, HPR ID and HPID. They are the same thing.

A facility manager is not an HPR category. It is the person who
registers a facility in the Health Facility Registry, and they use a
Healthcare Professional ID to do it. An earlier version of this entry
listed facility managers as if HPR held them, and it does not.

An earlier version also called the Healthcare Professional ID a
fourteen digit identifier. No fetched NHA page states its length, so
the claim is removed rather than repeated.
output.summary: The registry of individual healthcare professionals across every system of medicine, which issues a Healthcare Professional ID.
output.title: HPR, Healthcare Professionals Registry

reply.Text:
A **health professional ID (HPID)** is a 14-digit digital identifier issued to healthcare professionals in India's ABDM ecosystem. Here are the key points:

**What it is:**
- A unique identifier for a healthcare professional's digital identity across ABDM
- Issued by the Healthcare Professionals Registry (HPR) after Aadhaar authentication

**Who gets one:**
- Doctors from any system of medicine (modern medicine, dentistry, Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa, homeopathy)
- Nurses and pharmacists
- Also used by facility managers registering facilities in the Health Facility Registry

**Key details:**
- Registration is voluntary and free
- It does not replace the professional's existing registration with their medical council—the councils remain the authority
- HPR verifies professionals against their respective councils
- The identifier is sometimes also called "HPR ID" or "Healthcare Professional ID" interchangeably

**When you need it:**
- You cannot use an HPID before the professional has completed Aadhaar authentication with HPR
- It's required for any subsequent ABDM operations by that professional

See the [ABDM glossary](/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#hpid) for details.
